reviews.review_title: You get what you pay for...in this case, very little.
reviews.review_text: Good:<br>- Close proximity to restaurants, bars and Mill Street shops.<br>- Pools and laundry facilities are never crowded.<br>- Maintenance staff fix problems quickly, without any quibbles.<br>- Cheap, for Tempe.  Our "junior one-bed" was $519 per month - just over $606, with all the utilities etc.<br><br>Bad:<br>- If you don't like cockroaches, don't move here! The complex has a cockroach problem and although we kept our apartment extremely clean, kept all the plugholes stopped up and sprayed Raid around, we still had trouble with them. We were told to expect to see some when we moved to Arizona, but we didn't expect to see quite as many as this.  The worst was when one crawled up my pant leg - in broad daylight, as I was sitting at my computer.  We also found an egg sac in the closet (unhatched, fortunately - a dozen baby roaches would have come out of there!).  I went to see the staff about this and they put our apartment on a list of apts., for a pest control man to come round and spray the place.  They said he came every week to do this.  I didn't know if this was a good thing or a bad thing!  It seemed to me that the roaches were just circulating around the building - when they were sprayed out of one apt., they moved onto other apts., and so on.<br>- This area suffers from vehicle crime.  Police cars were often present in the parking lots during the day and the night.  When we moved here we bought bikes but other residents advised us against keeping them outside, in the cycle ranks.     <br>- The apts were small and poky.  Our "junior one bed" was a 450 sq ft room with a half wall in the middle.<br>- When we moved in we were told that the majority of residents were students and young professionals.  But it seemed to us that many of the people here were section 8.<br>- Another resident told us that there was a drug problem here.  I didn't experience anything to support that claim.  Although there was a lot of door-knocking and brawling late at night.<br><br>To those moving to Tempe for the first time: why don't you look at Mesa?  You can get much more bang for your buck there, and cities round here all look the same anyway.

reviews.author: Current Resident 938727
reviews.review_text: I would NOT recommend this complex. I rented a studio apartment for a good price for the location (and quiet community), but had several problems that caused me to enjoy the experience less and less. First, maintenance never responded when called, other than to inform me that they received my request. Additionally, the water in my particular unit was shut off almost weekly for pipe repairs, though it was not on a consistent schedule and I was only informed the first two times it was shut-off--after that it was a gamble as to whether or not the water would be working when I got up for work/school. Second, the turnover rate for management is ridiculously small: every time I walked in the office (at least once a month) the entire staff was new, which caused problem when it came to reporting to me the CORRECT rent amount due per month and when answering questions. The complex decided to go "paperless" at about month #2 into my lease and yet never sent out a properly functioning, complete e-mail. After about month #4 I receive no e-mail whatsoever and could only ever be told how much I owed for rent if I was able to walk in to the office and talk to someone (heaven forbid someone answers the office phone once in a while). Also, the "great deal" I was offered and pestered about to resign my lease was at least $50 MORE than what I had been paying for rent. Thirdly, though the complex seems nice and is quiet, lights are often broken, the apartments themselves are old and therefore break easily (I was down to a single, half-functioning stovetop coil and a from door that would not close completely by the time I moved), and a few crimes have occurred in and around the complex (possibly because of how dark it is). It is liveable and semi-safe, but I would definitely keep and eye peeled for safety hazards associated with both the shady neighborhood and the old appliances/apartments. Also, do not trust any staff member that tells you that the apartment is "old and worn" and that in general they will be a bit more lenient on the condition of the carpet, walls, and other features--I cleaned my tub/shower to a point that it was cleaner than when I moved in, yet I was charged for a "dirty tub". Fourth and final, if you do have to move in I do not recommend getting a pet or bringing a pet in. I adopted a cat and brought him in to the apartment, paid the fee and monthly pet fee, only to find out after moving out that the pet fee covered absolutely no damages done to the apartment by the pet as with other residences, but merely any instances of urine outside in the courtyard. I don't know about you, but a $100 fee plus $35 a month seems like a steep cost for urine in grass. I was not once informed of this when I initially adopted the pet and talked to office staff. I also must add that while most of the time the staff was friendly (though generally not helpful), there were a few times that I encountered condescending staff  members.

The rent and included utilities are AMAZING. That's the main reason we went with this apartment complex. We have had several other problems structure wise that we have put in tickets for, but have not been fixed or approached in MONTHS. The ceiling in the bathroom looks like it's going to give out from the tub on the second floor, door hinges have been broken since move in, stove coils have been non-working since move in, outlets are EXTREMELY loose and unsafe to use without surge protectors, and cupboards/drawers in the kitchen and bathroom are severely damaged and warped and don't stay closed..

We've stopped going to the onsite laundry facility, and started using the one across the street (which we've noticed a LOT of the residents have started doing.

Most of the neighbors are alcoholics and spend the week nights screaming at the top of their lungs and pounding on/kicking doors and slamming them. It's ridiculous. HORRIBLE customer service! :(

The maintenance guy is friendly. He's really the only staff member we like. :) (I find it very odd that a complex as big as this is, that there is ONLY ONE guy doing ALL of the maintenance.. 

Overall: If you are living by yourself or are a single couple looking for a one bedroom and can get into the Sierra Vista I side, then you should be okay and I recommend this facility. However, if you have a family or are looking for a place with friends, GO SOMEWHERE ELSE.. :/

I have lived in Sierra Vista 1 for two years. 

Pros:
I love the location: 10-minute drive to Sky Harbor Airpot, 5 minutes from ASU by car or bus or 15 minutes walking. 4 bus routes go by the nearest intersection: Red Line which can take you to campus or to the airport no need to call a cab, a shuttle or bug someone to drop you off or pick you up), 30, 44, and 62, all of which go by ASU. Cons
The apartments are old and a bit overpriced. However as of this month electricity is no longer included, so you might find a better deal somewhere else. Occasionally you might see a roach and need management to send someone to your place to spray it. With all the parking space available, surprisingly few spots are covered and you have to pay extra for covered parking. 

Overall, I don't think it's that bad. I think it's good for people who don't need the latest fanciest most fashionable place. I'd totally recommend it if they had the electricity deal going on. Now I think you might find a better deal elsewhere. Not so bad over all though. I'm moving out of state and saying good bye to Sierra Vista for good.

reviews.author: canonlyhope22
reviews.review_title: Air Conditioning Down 28 Days and Counting
reviews.review_text:
UPDATE ON SITUATION AND PHOTOS 09/20/2010 







Office DOES NOT return phone calls, that is if you can get hold of the office staff and not the answering service when calling during business hours.
Someone had busted the light and trashed the main laundry room,clothes were thrown all over the place. The laundry money machine was broken into,laundry company was here today handling the matter. In the smaller 
Animal feces in front yards.



Dropped off a list of repairs that are still waiting to be finished, some dating back to our original move in date. Office manager stated that someone from maintenance would have to stop by and look,today being Monday and still waiting.

Put in a a couple of calls to the office today, first time the call was answered by answering service(call was put in at approximately 1pm this afternoon), having been put on hold for more than five minutes I hung up and decided to call back later. 
      Placed call to office about an half and hour later, and was told by the office staff member that answered the phone that the office manager was busy, left a message and number for the office manager to call me back. 
            I just got off the phone with the manger(as almost four hours should have been sufficient time to return a phone call) When I spoke with the manager the answer for why I have not received a call as yet was "Oh, I thought someone had already called you." Do you not know? I asked about the other issues listed and was asked "which ones?" I mentioned the list of repairs that was dropped off on Thursday and was told "Yes I have that paper" at least they know what needs to be done.

Supposedly a member of maintenance will be by today to take a look at the situations, once they are done with the service call that they are currently working on.

Maybe it is just me but, I tend to not trust what I have been told.



The main air conditioning unit broke down on 17 July called to the office and was told it was the main portion of the unit and would be in working order that night (Saturday) called the next morning and was told will be up by that evening (Sunday) called the next day and was told that the main unit was fixed but, had caused issues with individual units. On Monday 20 July 2010 we placed a work order maintenance came out two days later and told us all we needed was a filter and that they were on order and would be in a day or two. Three days later when no filter shows I call again and am told they are still waiting for them to come in. I called every other day to see if they were in, they were not. Finally, after calling for almost two weeks I call and I am told the filters were in and one would be brought to my apartment, which it was within one half hour. We replace the filter and think that it will take at least a few hours if not overnight for the apartment to cool down.
 The next morning our apartment was still eighty five degrees, even while running two box fans, two desk fans and a mini turbo fan.
Once again I call the office and was told that maintenance would come by first thing the next morning. Which they did, they proceeded to clean the system and we were told that after they were done and a few hours wait we would start feeling the cool air. still 85
 Once again I call up to the office they send down another maintenance guy who says it is the thermostat it is not working properly so he will order the part. He does tell me he is not sure when it will be in but he will order the part. Okay
I called the office a few times last week to see if the part was in, of course not yet. I called yesterday( Monday) and was told that the part was in and she would get a hold of maintenance and call me back. Needless to say I did not get a call back.
Today Tuesday 17 August three days shy of a month with no remedy in sight. I call the office and get the answering service it is 9:05am the office is supposed to be open. So I wait and call again at 11:12am again the answering service. Okay so maybe there was an issue I would call later.At 3:29pm I called and got the office and asked to speak to a manager was told they were out to lunch and I would get a call when they returned. Having not received a call by 4:40pm, I called again was asked to hold then while on hold for several minutes was asked to hold again, this time a few minutes, when the phone was picked up, I was told that it was going to be a while so I would get a call back. I said I wanted a call back before the office closed for the day. Needless to say I did not receive one back.
Now, I can understand there are many things involved when managing a property. It upsets me that now I have the feeling that we are just getting the run around. We pay our rent on time abide by the rules, and respect our neighbors. I had mentioned to both management as well as maintenance that this is not just a comfort issue but, a health risk as well. I know I may be sounding a bit snippy but since this situation has been going on Tempe has been issued several excessive heat WARNINGS. One of the thing they tell you to do is stay indoors where it is cool Well, my indoors are not cool.
We are just about at our wits end with this place The turnover of staff both office and maintenance seems to be a deterrent to resolving these issues.
I am honestly worried as to what is going to "break down" next.
I feel we have been more than patient up to this point but, we are getting tired of things not being done something really has to be done.


UPDATE ON SITUATION 05/26/2010


New Property manager has been open to listening to issues with apartment. As of the posting of this review the roach situation is being remedied, seems there was a small hole behind the refrigerator as well as a metal plate that was loose under the sink that was where the roaches were gaining entrance into the apartment. Seems as if the roaches had traveled from another apartment and the property manager has assured me that she will look into the situation. Maintenance filled the holes and the exterminator has been out to spray. Seems to be working so far we are seeing less roaches in the apartment. Several other issues that we had notified the apartment manager of have either already been taken care of or are in the process of resolving. Hopefully things will continue to improve.
I still would suggest touring the actual apartment you will be renting before signing a lease.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Unfortunately it has been one thing after another. First off got a call the night before our move that our apartment would not be ready for the date agreed upon at the signing of our lease. So okay how is this issue solved? Received a call back later on the night and to remedy the situation we would be given an apartment other than the original one, no problem...or so we thought.
 Due to the fact that we were moving ourselves we did not actually see more of the apartment other than the time we were going in and dropping off our boxes. I know I should have looked over the apartment but, at the time we had a deadline on which we had to meet to get our rental truck back.
 So we finally settle in and the first thing that greets us are roaches, in our bathroom kitchen and later on the evening even in our bedroom. So we call the office (note it is now after hours so we get the service) and inform them of the situation. The next morning we get a call saying we will be first on the list to have an exterminator spray...4 days from the time we called. We were told when they did arrive that they would have to come every week for a while and possibly bomb. I do not know but, I would imagine all that should have been done prior to anyone moving in. Okay so we figure lets try the weekly spraying and go from there. Needless to say they did not show this week so the problem is NOT getting under control.
 We also gave the rental office a list of repairs that need doing over a week ago and they have fixed one of the issues listed yesterday We were told that maintenance would be by today as well to take care of the other issues they never showed.
 We are hoping this is a rare occurrence and that ALL the issues will be remedied in a timely manner.. 
If you are going to rent here I would strongly suggest that you make sure you see the actual apartment you will be renting before you sign a lease.

reviews.review_text:
Nobody on this site ever uses this to give balanced review.  They mainly use it for revenge over a slight from management.  Don't get me wrong, there is a lot to be desired living here and dealing with the management (both past and present).  Overall, I like where I am living but I have a very well placed unit.  

Here are my observations:

-Never seen any roaches, and hardly any bugs for that matter (2nd floor apt, kept clean)

-Maintenance will respond to problems though sometimes you have to pester the office to get them to follow through.  UPDATE: This got REALLY bad for a time and then they worked on a big fix.  I will add updates as I see how they proceed under the new system they said they were following.

-I don't like some of the comments made in other reviews about races hear.  I see low income tenants with kids, lots of whom are minorities.  Calling the place    ------ seems like racial profiling to me and assumptive.  Just because someone is black, doesn't have a lot of money and has kids, doesn't make it ------.  Still, every once in while some ------- drives through or parks with his car stereo blasting rap and then even I think it's ------, but half the time that's some white kid from white suburbia.  It is not that bad nor frequent though.

-Cops are here a lot but in Tempe they are everywhere (Tempe voters approve every debt inducing bond project lobbied for by emergency services).  If you personally have a problem, they will be here quick and that is what is important.

-Air Conditioning: here they are challenged.  They have a crappy chiller unit that has never worked right.  HOWEVER; at huge expense to them, they have hooked up a massive temporary unit, which as of this writing is working ALMOST perfectly.  We have yet to see how well the system works when the new permanent chiller is fixed/replaced.  It has been a living hell the few time the a/c has gone down, but they usually get it back up fast.  We are talking less than 1 day turn around but an event that occurs often twice per summer.  UPDATE: This may have been fixed this summer but my unit still seemed challenged.  But my unit has windows catching rays both in the morning and evening.  I have had to seal my windows with thermal insulation and use portable A/C units to compensate.  Summer 2010 will be the real test of the new chiller system.

Now, first off, let me say that I did not hate living here. I'm a very poor college student who liked the price range and the fact that all utilities were included except water. The staff was pretty nice to me most of the time. I think my day-to-day living experience might have been better because I was right next to the office & surrounded by college students or quiet people. My biggest complaints about living there were the crusty carpets and the HUGE roach problem. Even if you could kill them off, there were roach carcasses everywhere. It sucked.

Now, that being said, I can't really report this place/area being safe. One night after I got home from work, a stranger followed me into my apartment. I defended myself and he clocked me pretty good and then left. I dont know if he wanted to rob me, or rape me or was just a high individual but I'm glad neither happened. The police were called and i was in shock for a while. I know it's not the staff's fault but it was a really bad thing to have happened. 

When I went to the office the next day to let them know I was going to need to go. And I think they meant well, but they really questioned me about what happened and it was in front of the whole staff and other residents. It was really embarrassing and I was upset that they did that. They didn't even know (or were informed) at all that a resident had been attacked in an apartment so close to the office when there had been around 10 cops there the night before. Though Yvonne (who I've actually known from when I lived in another complex) I am sure was just very genuinely concerned. She wanted to know what the person looked like so she could keep an eye out. But these were kind of things I was not ready to share with everyone else.

Again, not the staff's fault. Yvonne, Matt and Ryan (i think thats his name) were always pretty kind to me. The apartments aren't great by any means but you get what you pay for and it's great for college students. Believe it or not, I would recommend it. reviews.review_text: I have lived at the Sierra Vista Apartments for two years now, and it is not nearly as bad as most of the reviews on this site make it out to be. reviews.author: mookaoman
reviews.review_text:
Sierra Vista Apartments are terrible. This was my first experience living on my own, so when they rushed me through the walk through and all that, I didn't think a thing of it. We thought it looked pretty ok when we first saw it. It looked average, nothing special, but definetly not horrible.
First of all, there is a huge roach problem. The roaches pretty much rule the place...normally roaches are afraid of humans/light, but I have woken up in the middle of the night from roaches crawling on me. They are very used to being here. I have tried everything from roach spray, to traps, to bug bombing the place, and have been keeping it very clean. I still have bug problems, but have managed to keep it semi-tolerable. 
Also, weird electrical problems, I have a feeling something is screwy as far as that goes. There have been two fires in other units in the last 4 months we have lived here, one was literally two doors down. Not only that, but every time my room mate or I have tried to clean the stove, we get a mini electrical shock up our arm...like one that is strong enough to make me pull away and jump across the room. 
Once a month or so, the water shuts off for no reason at all, no notice...which can be really inconvenient if I plan to take a shower before work or school. I will call the leasing office, and they always say "They are doing maintenance , it will be about 3 hours...". 
Another thing, the dishwasher is crap. It doesn't wash our dishes, it sloshes soap on them and leaves soap residue. We rinse our dishes well before loading the washer. 
Other gross things that were noted when moving in...randomly finding gobs of hair in the dishwasher, and sink, and another unidentifiable cruddy substance. I am starting to notice that all over the walls there is hair that has been painted over, in several places, in several rooms, as well as other weird chunks (painted over of course), that don't look like they are part of the kind of texture on the wall.
There are a lot of neighbors who are loud and noisy, a lot of druggies that hang out here too. There are also a lot of people with loud, noisy kids. I found out from my neighbors that crackheads used to live in the unit we're currently in. 
Our rent is an amazing price, and our utilities (except water) are included, but it isn't worth it to live in a crappy place. The landlords here are ding dongs, this management company doesn't know how to hire people. The first main landlord was a complete jerk to us every time we told him we had an issue, and basically brushed aside all our issues, and then he was fired. This new lady is such a flake, that we had to pay our water bill a month early because she screwed up something with their account with the city of Tempe (according to the Leasing office, which they tried to blame on the post office). Point of this whole drabble is, that these guys run you around in circles and stick you with a crappy deal. 
They screwed us into signing a 13 month lease, because they were going to charge us $150 more per month if we decided to only sign a 6 month lease. Don't live here if you can help it. If its a must for some reason (like cost, for instance), get a unit on the side close to the leasing office, it is cleaner, better maintained, and it generally looks better. Plus the laundromat on that side costs less.

reviews.author: Current Resident 556677
reviews.review_text:
I rented a studio from May-November 2013. I waited to post this review until I received my deposit back, which took over a month and many, many calls to the office. This place is one of the worst apartment complexes out there. It had to have been built in the 60's.

Overall apartment: Upon move-in, our entire move-in checklist was filled with problems and we had at least 35-40 urgent maintenance requests. This alerted the property manager who came to our apartment to review our requests. The work orders were put in and everything was "completed" in the next few days but nothing was repaired accordingly. The towel racks were hanging out of the wall so they extended the bars and "patched" the holes in the walls with general caulking. Are you serious??? The caulking was never covered with paint and was an eye sore to look at. EVERYTHING is painted over after each new tenant. This includes all the electrical plate covers, the breaker box, door/cabinet hinges, the sink stopper. Good luck trying to open/close things properly. All the cabinet door don't close right or completely, we asked for this to be fixed and maintenance refused. The cabinet door in the bathroom fell off the hinges and they just moved the hinge further down the door instead of fixing it properly. The paint in the bathroom tub starting peeling off about a month before our move-out. The toilet is so small it should belong in a daycare bathroom, and the door just barely closes past the toilet- no wonder why they couldn't have a regular sized toilet. The tub is what makes me certain this apartment was built in the 60's. It's not long enough for me (a 5'4" women) to completely stretch my legs out in. The shower liner was detaching from the wall and cracked (a moisture hazard). You can tell it was patched over with their famous general caulking but that didn't help anything.

Appliances: The same stove has been in the apartment since it was built because it is impossible to even pull completely out from the counter. It was FILTHY underneath and behind, and the cleaning lady said nothing could be done because it can't be moved. EWWW!! The knobs on the range never worked. We had to use pliers to turn off the knobs. The oven constantly burned our food because it was far too old to properly function. The vent above the stove never functioned and the fan was stuck on for about an hour our first night because we couldn't turn it off. There is no microwave and no place to put one on the counter if you buy one. We constantly were moving our small appliances off the counter just to do dishes, in the very small sink.

Flooring: Don't let them fool you if they say you will have "wood" flooring in your apartment. It is the cheapest linoleum there is and was coming up by the time we left, but they told us it was new. The carpet is awfully warn out and stained. It is well past needing to be replaced. Our feet were dirty after walking on it every night until we took the money to clean it, I guess it was our responsibility to clean it??

Lighting: There is one light in the living area and it doesn't provide even adequate light. Be prepared to buy some lamps. The fan was practically coming out of the ceiling when we moved in and it was tightened by maintenance. The fan blades have been painted on and never cleaned. The fan in the bathroom sounded like a lawnmower and we ended up just unplugging it after maintenance put in a "new" one that was even worse.

Safety/noise: Our neighbor was definitely dealing drugs out of his apartment and he always allowed his visitors to stand outside our apartment and smoke. Which was nice since it came through our A/C unit and made our whole apartment reek. We were asked on multiple occasions for money from his "guests". He also busted his window out and the management has allowed it to remain that way for over a month. I wonder how long they'll let that continue. The parking is not well lit and the lights were completely out for about 2 weeks on our building and the buildings around us. We lived next to the stairs on the first floor and the dishes in the cabinets would rattle when someone walked up or down the stairs. The police and fire sirens are constantly going off at all hours of the day. The windows are single paned and have a very simple latch to close that could have easily been broken into. We asked for a more security and they gave us another small screw device that goes on the track of the window. Because that's going to stop a whole lot..

Office staff: Oh my.... The office staff had a turnover rate of about two weeks and someone new would be there every time I went into the office. The people working there would speak Spanish to each other when talking about what I was asking them, which I found incredibly rude and inconsiderate. I think some of them just honestly didn't know English. When I would get a package, no one in the office had the intelligence to be able to find it and I would always have to point it out from across the room. I finally was done dealing with them and would just go pick it out of the pile myself. Maintenance requests were never entered into the system correctly or with enough detail for the maintenance staff to handle the request correctly. One of us always had to be at the apartment for the repairs to explain. But it didn't matter, the requests weren't completed properly, just enough to regain minimal function regardless of how it looked in the end.

Amenities: What amenities? You'll see on the website beautiful landscaping and pools. The main pool was green, as in it looked like a lake, for almost a month in the middle of the summer. It takes that long to get a pool's water back to normal? How about drain it and start over at that point? They never did.. We were given the key to the pool across the road (how convenient!) which was full of bugs, leaves, dirt and kids that weren't with their parents (that is the 2 bedroom side of the complex). We didn't swim in any pool after that. There is a fitness center smaller than the studio and I didn't want to pay for a key to use it. The onsite laundry facilities were filthy and expensive to use. You had to pay a deposit on a card and then load the card during business hours, which was very inconvenient. There is also an "Internet cafe" with a coffee machine that is always turned off. The printer doesn't work and if you want anything printed off you must email it to the manager who prints it off in the office (nothing like a little privacy, right??). There is no landscaping unless you count dirt where there used to be grass. The bushes are all overgrown and there is trash thrown down next to them.

The pros: There are a few.. Our electric was covered under the rent so we could use as much as we wanted, and we sure did take advantage of it! The water is billed based on how many people live in the apartment, not on usage, so again we took advantage of that. We were always able to park right outside our apartment. We never had a big issue with bugs even though they never sprayed the inside of the apartment.

I've been waiting a very long time to write this review. I don't want anyone else to get suckered into this apartment like we were. We were way too naive when we moved in here. Please always look at the apartment you are going to be living in before moving in. The models always look better and that's an understatement in this case. I am so happy to be out of here. Please stay away from this place. There are so many better apartments in Tempe for the price.

My boyfriend and I have been living here for a little over a year. We came here initially because the rent was so cheap - we got a two bedroom apartment for $575/mo, with electricity included. It sounded like a fantastic deal until I realized that we are getting what we paid for. Here is a short list of the problems with this complex:

1. First and foremost, the NOISE! I'm not sure if the walls are made out of cardboard or some other equally cheap/noise-conducive material, but we hear EVERYTHING! Planes flying in and out of Sky Harbor at pretty much all hours, trains blasting their whistles in the middle of the night, drunk people hanging out in the greenbelt area shouting, neighbors screaming at each other and their kids . . . we've experimented with various combos of bed placement/ear plugs to mitigate the noise and its still terrible.


2. Plumbing issues. There is currently a river of sewage right outside my apartment, and our water has been shut off intermittently at various points over the last couple of weeks. There is nothing more fun than waking up and realizing that you can't even shower or brush your teeth before work. I've tried calling the maintenance phone number, only to get blown off and ignored, so today I finally called the front office to complain, only to be told that I "should be relieved my electricity is still working" because lots of residents have had both their electricity AND water shut off due to maintenance problems. What a reassuring thing to hear from the front office! Let me be clear here - this is NOT a one-time plumbing emergency. We have had our water shut off three times during the day in the last two weeks, and who knows how many other times it was shut off while we weren't at home. There seem to be broken pipes constantly, since that's the excuse the front office and maintenance people give to explain both the water shut-offs and the river of sewage right outside my apartment.

3. Other residents - let's just say the neighbors are colorful. Fortunately, two of the worst (a drug dealer and an abusive mom who screamed at her children at all hours of the night) have moved out or have been evicted recently. Still, it's not at all surprising to see police cars here constantly. 

If you can afford better, DO NOT LIVE HERE! I cannot wait until our lease is up!

I would just like to finally take the time to say something. The past year living at Sierra Vista has been in one word, miserable. I take pride in being a very calm, thoughtful and understanding individual and I have been nothing but that until now.
      The water situation as of lately has been hard to handle.  We (myself and my family) went over three weeks without hot water.
